content: Major Cdk9-interacting elongation factor (MCEF), also referred to as AFF4 or AF5q31, is a transcription factor that is closely related to the AF4 family of transcription factors. It represents the fourth member of the AF4 family (AFF), which is implicated in a variety of pathological conditions. These include Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL), abnormal central nervous system (CNS) development, breast cancer, and azoospermia. MCEF has been shown to interact with the species-specific human co-factor P-TEFb, which is essential for HIV-1 transcription. Additionally, it has the ability to repress HIV-1 replication. Due to these properties, MCEF holds potential for future therapeutic applications, particularly in the context of HIV-1 treatment. The MCEF gene was originally cloned and named by Mario Clemente Estable during his tenure as a post-doctoral fellow in the laboratory of Robert G. Roeder at Rockefeller University.
